attachments.document_title: Proof of the date the notice was received
attachments.label: A1
must_show: how it was delivered (registered-mail tracking, envelope or acknowledgement)
attachments.text:
From: Leo Widmer, Lindenmatt Management Ltd
To: Laura Fankhauser
Date: 2 February 2026
Subject: Your query

Dear Ms Fankhauser,

Further to your call, I confirm that our letter concerning your flat at Mühleweg 34, Schaffhausen, was received by you on 15 January 2026. This is also the date recorded in our files.

If you have further questions about the contents of the letter, please put them to us in writing so that we can answer them properly.

Kind regards,
Leo Widmer
Lindenmatt Management Ltd

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

text:
Hello,

I've rented a flat at Mühleweg 34 in Schaffhausen from Lindenmatt Management Ltd since 2022. My lease has never had anything linking the rent to the consumer price index or any other index, so whatever is going on now, it isn't that.

What I'm not sure about is a side agreement I signed in February 2023 when we added a garden seating area. It says something about the rent rising by set amounts "in stages", but it's vague and doesn't give clear dates. I can't tell whether what's happening now is one of those stages. My partner Chris Bucher thinks it is; Mr Leo Widmer at Lindenmatt told me on the phone it has nothing to do with it. Neither of us really knows.

Anyway, the letter from Lindenmatt says my rent goes up from CHF 3270 to CHF 3520 a month from 1 May 2026.

I've attached Lindenmatt's own confirmation of the date I received it, which was 15 January 2026.

The part that really shocked me: in the same envelope there was also a notice terminating my lease at the end of June. So they announced a higher rent and terminated me at the same time. I'm still trying to understand what that is supposed to mean.

The reasons on the rent form are that Lindenmatt renovated all the kitchens in the building last autumn, which I can confirm, and that their mortgage costs have gone up. I don't see why I should pay for a kitchen I didn't ask for, especially if I'm being put out anyway.

What are my options here?

Best regards,
Laura Fankhauser
